vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: widgetkit-code-review
Version: 1.2.0

The skill bundle is a legitimate set of reference materials and instructions for performing WidgetKit code reviews. It contains technical documentation and checklists regarding TimelineProvider, App Intents, performance optimization, and view composition (SKILL.md, references/*.md). No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found; all code snippets and instructions are standard Swift/iOS development practices.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only WidgetKit code-review checklist and reference bundle; its requirements and instructions are consistent with that purpose and it requests no credentials or installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the content: the skill provides checklists and detailed references for WidgetKit timelines, views, intents, and performance. It requests no unrelated binaries, env vars, or config paths.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the reference files contain review guidance and code samples for WidgetKit only. They do not instruct the agent to read system files, access environment variables, call external endpoints, or perform actions outside code review scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files to execute; this is instruction-only so nothing will be written to disk or fetched during installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The guidance references only app-level constructs (App Groups, widget config) that are appropriate to WidgetKit reviews.

llm.guidance: This skill is a reference/checklist for reviewing WidgetKit Swift code and appears internally consistent and low-risk: it asks for nothing external and has no install steps. Before using, avoid pasting secrets or user private data into the code you ask the skill to review (API keys, auth tokens, or PII), and remember that while the skill itself is inert, an autonomous agent using it may request or inspect any code you feed it — review what you submit. If you need the skill to run on private repositories, prefer sharing minimal, redacted examples rather than full credentials.
